newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market eyes Bundesbank, trade sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market eyes Bundesbank, trade sluggish.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were mostly flat in sluggish Wednesday trade.

Only call money moved, slipping a few basis points. It was quoted at 2.75 to 2.81 bid and changed hands between 2.81 and 2.88 percent, dealers said. They said the lower overnight rate did not have a fundamental reason as the market was very calm.
Dealers noted some activity in the longer segment, with one-year deposits unchanged at 3.05/13 percent bid/ask and most deals done near 3.13 percent.
They said the market was closely watching the Bundesbank for signs of a repo cut on Thursday.
But they said the chances of the Dutch following with a cut in the equivalent special advances rate were very small.
"It seems unlikely that the central bank will adjust its special advances rate tomorrow. But if it does, it will hike the rate a little," a dealer said.
Another dealer agreed, saying a rate move was unlikely. But he added that if there was a change, it would be a 10-basis point hike to 2.60 percent.
One dealer said he only saw technical reasons for the central bank to hike the rate. He said the gap between the special advances rate and the AIBOR was relatively wide.
One-month AIBOR was quoted at 2.88/95, and the special advances rate has been pegged at 2.50 percent for months.
But the dealer said if the central bank did lift the special advance rate, it would also have to move other rates, which was seen leading to guilder unrest.
A failure to follow the Bundesbank down would lead to a reduction in the gap between market and official rates, he said.
